question: What is Morgan Stanley's strategy to increase their net new assets?

claims.text: On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), CEO Ted Pick said investments in the self-directed and Workplace channels drive Wealth Management's differentiated client acquisition funnel. He said the firm reaches over 19 million relationships and added net new assets of over $250 billion in each of the past two years, on track to $10 trillion plus of total client assets.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), Pick said Wealth has three channels (financial advisors, Workplace and E*TRADE), each a category leader, which together make up the firm's 'strategic client acquisition model'. He said Wealth Management had net new assets of over $350 billion last year and, over five years, $1.6 trillion plus of net new assets with a doubling of fee-based flows. The 2025 10-K reports 2025 net new assets of $356 billion.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), management said its intentional strategy is to introduce and educate retail clients on the value of advice. Management cited the EquityZen acquisition, an expanded Carta partnership and a Zero Hash collaboration as foundations for 'sustainable growth to widen our competitive moats'.

On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Pick said the client acquisition funnel will continue to drive Wealth Management's performance. He said the firm seeks, 'with the passage of time', to grow stand-alone wealth assets from the current $8 trillion to $10 trillion. CFO Sharon Yeshaya credited 'sustained investments in our client acquisition funnel' with reaching more clients and deepening existing relationships.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Pick described the 'integrated scaling of the funnel' as a critical strategic matter. He listed the self-directed channel, a differentiated and expanding workplace offering, and trust-based relationships between financial advisers and clients, with technology as a differentiator.

Workplace (1Q25 call, April 2025): Yeshaya said an incremental $20 billion migrated from workplace to the advisor-led channel in the quarter, adding to roughly $300 billion accumulated since the channel was expanded in 2020.

Workplace (2Q25 call, July 2025): Yeshaya said 70% of the flows that originate from workplace are net new assets to the firm. She also said workplace-originated flows were running ahead of the roughly $16 billion per year previously cited.

Workplace (3Q25 call, October 2025): Yeshaya said workplace is 'probably the most exciting part' and that the firm is 'just scratching the surface'. She said IPO-driven assets arrive in self-directed accounts and also move directly into advisor-led accounts.

Workplace (4Q25 call, January 2026): management said advisor-led assets originating from workplace and E*TRADE relationships grew to a record $99 billion for the full year, against historical averages of around $60 billion per year.

Workplace (2Q26 call, July 2026): Pick said the record $148 billion of net new assets was driven by large IPOs of late-stage private workplace clients, which he called a cornerstone of the client acquisition funnel. Yeshaya said stock plan IPO flows were just over half of NNA.

Workplace (3Q26 call, October 2026): Yeshaya said fee-based flows of $80 billion included a corporate retirement mandate that supplied nearly half. She said the firm continues to expand its retirement capabilities and deepen engagement with plan participants.

Financial advisor productivity and recruiting (1Q25 call, April 2025): Yeshaya said Q1 net new assets were supported by advisor-led clients, stock plan vesting, 'positive recruiting trends' and self-directed clients. Pick said that at the top of the funnel it is about the financial advisor, citing the firm's access to intellectual capital, technology and compensation viewed as fair. He said the firm is selective but gets a lot of inbound inquiry.

Financial advisor productivity and recruiting (2Q25 call, July 2025): Yeshaya said advisor-led flows were particularly strong. She said they came from new advisors attracted by the strength of workplace, as well as from assets that originated in workplace. Advisor-led flows also came from existing advisors and recruits.

Financial advisor productivity (4Q25 call, January 2026): Pick said the firm is using its scale to broaden advisor capabilities that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending. He said $100 billion migrated to financial advisors in 2025.

E*TRADE / self-directed (2Q25 call, July 2025): Yeshaya said self-directed flows improved year over year, which she credited to investments in marketing and business development and new tools such as E*TRADE Pro. On the 3Q25 call (October 2025) she said the firm was increasing marketing and business development in self-directed. Pick said on the 1Q25 call that the firm is investing in E*TRADE.

Referrals from Institutional Securities and the integrated firm (3Q25 call, October 2025): Yeshaya said workplace and IPO activity are ways to build out the integrated firm. She said the firm has people to shepherd individuals across institutional securities and underwriting, and that there is 'a lot more to go'.

Referrals from Institutional Securities and the integrated firm (4Q25 call, January 2026): management said Q4 net new assets of $122 billion had contributions across all channels. Growth was 'supported by institutional relationships related to the integrated firm'.

Referrals from Institutional Securities and the integrated firm (2Q26 call, July 2026): Pick said that with institutional activity strong and IPO markets open, the firm 'connected the Integrated Firm to translate institutional strength into client value through our adviser-led and E*TRADE channels'. He said the firm led landmark IPOs in the quarter.

Net new assets were $251.7 billion in FY2024 and $356.3 billion in FY2025. Fee-based asset flows were $123.1 billion in FY2024 and $160.1 billion in FY2025. Quarterly net new assets for 4Q25 were $122.3 billion against $56.5 billion in 4Q24.

Management's 2025 quarterly commentary: 1Q25 net new assets were $94 billion, a 6% annualized growth rate of beginning-period assets (April 2025 call). 2Q25 net new assets were $59 billion, strong despite higher seasonal tax payments (July 2025 call). 3Q25 net new assets were $81 billion, with all three channels contributing and the reopening of the IPO market supporting results (October 2025 call).

2026 results: net new assets were $118 billion in 1Q26 and a record $148 billion in 2Q26, of which just over half represented IPO-related inflows in the Workplace channel. They were a record $232 billion in 3Q26, again with just over half associated with IPO-related flows. In the first nine months of 2026, management said it delivered roughly $0.5 trillion of net new assets and about $175 billion in fee-based flows.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Yeshaya said an active IPO calendar accelerates the pace of the funnel. She cautioned that 'flows will fluctuate as lockups expire, funds make distributions and individuals use assets for consumption'. She said the pipeline and connectivity across channels let the firm build relationships early and deepen them over time.

The stated asset goals are $10 trillion plus of total client assets, cited on the 4Q24 call (January 2025). On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Pick said total client assets across Wealth and Investment Management had reached $10 trillion. He also said the firm seeks to grow stand-alone wealth assets from $8 trillion to $10 trillion. These are asset-level goals, not annual NNA targets.

Management's own caution on drivers: the 2025 10-K says NNA is influenced by macro factors, seasonality, the firm's ability to attract and retain financial advisors and clients, capital market and corporate activities, and large idiosyncratic inflows and outflows. It adds that 'should these factors continue, the growth rate of our NNA may be impacted.' The 2Q26 10-Q (August 2026) repeats this and adds single large client events.
Seasonal tax outflows: on the 2Q25 call (July 2025), management said Q2 net new assets of $59 billion were inclusive of a $22 billion headwind from tax outflows.

Client cash and deposit pricing: the 10-Qs for 2Q25 (August 2025) and 2Q26 (August 2026) say interest rate changes and other macroeconomic factors have affected client preferences, including cash allocation to other products. They also cite 'pricing changes to certain deposit types due to various competitive dynamics', which have affected net interest income. The 2Q26 filing says net interest income may be affected in future periods if these factors persist.

Cash sweep (1Q26 call, April 2026): Yeshaya said sweep balances have behaved with some yield-seeking behavior, and that the transactional nature of the cash is what 'you've seen bottom out' in the near term.

Competition and market risk (2025 10-K, February 2026): the firm lists commercial banks, global investment banks, regional banks, broker-dealers, private banks, registered investment advisers, digital investing platforms, asset managers and fintechs as competitors. It says it competes to attract and retain qualified employees. It also says unfavorable market or economic conditions could affect net new asset flows and flows into fee-based assets, which could hurt Wealth Management results.

gaps.what: No explicit annual or quarterly net-new-asset target or numeric growth-rate goal for Wealth Management was found. The stated goals are asset-level ($10 trillion plus total client assets; stand-alone wealth assets from $8 trillion to $10 trillion).
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley investor day or strategic update presentation, or management commentary on firm-wide Wealth Management goals

gaps.what: The effect of cash sweep or client cash behavior, or competitive deposit pricing, on net new assets is not quantified. The evidence addresses net interest income and sweep balances, not NNA.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley 10-Q/10-K deposit and sweep disclosures, earnings call Q&A on cash sweep and client cash allocation
